branches.name: West Circumferential Scout Highway (Dhelv to Šurpu-Dhelv)

caverns.name: Dhelv Great Bottle Hall
caverns.notes: Zeijani capital (pop ~5,000): 280x200 m bottle hall under a 32 m throat well, 3 satellite farm pits, stepwell cistern, Kailasa temple, and deep catacombs.

caverns.name: Dhelv West Kipuka Portal
caverns.notes: Hidden cliff portal and caravanserai in old-growth kipuka forest; guarded by a rolling stone door 2 km inside.

caverns.name: Deep Ossuary & Guanche Vaults
caverns.notes: 60 m below Dhelv square: tiered loculi, mummy shelves, and mortuary chapel.

caverns.name: Šurpu-Dhelv (Ash-Spire Village)
caverns.notes: First of the 3 canonical Mungo-sized Zeijani cave/tuff villages: fairy-chimney tuff spires and 4-level underground galleries above a braided lava tube.

caverns.name: Zey'danin Kipuka Sally Portal
caverns.notes: Concealed lava-tube mouth 12 km NE of Zey'danin used by Zeijani scouts and poison-arrow raiding parties.

caverns.name: Qarnu-Tūbu (Horn-Well Village)
caverns.notes: Second canonical Zeijani cave/tuff village: Moray-style terraced collapse pits and a Chand Baori stepwell cistern trading with the southern Ash Nomads.

caverns.name: Nūru-Šaplu (Deep-Lantern Village)
caverns.notes: Third canonical Zeijani cave village: carved into a drained parasitic magma chamber with Raufarholshellir red/purple oxidised basalt walls; center of alecap brewing and fungal alchemy.

caverns.name: Station 11 Three Skylights & Hot Reach
caverns.notes: Station 11 lava tube: 3 roof skylights with siphon trees and glow mushrooms upstream; active molten lava channel and CO2 sump downstream.

caverns.name: Entombed First Monastery Lava-Tube Vaults
caverns.notes: LORE.md 6.15: The original monastery of the Monks of History, buried under welded ignimbrite when the Lesser Throne erupted.

caverns.name: Pluton Pressurized Lava-Tube Galleries
caverns.notes: Insulated titanium-basalt lava tube halls at 9,650 m (0.50 atm) housing Pluton's deep mining works.

caverns.name: The Tubes Cavern Settlement
caverns.notes: Canonical cavern settlement (sa8xk6pimb) in a braided rift-shoulder lava-tube complex.

caverns.name: Loj Twenny Cavern
caverns.notes: Canonical cavern settlement (spbzmhdqqd) on the western rift rim.

name: Twins Caravan Pyroduct & Alph Headwater Conduit

branches.name: Caravan Pyroduct Cross-Range Route (Xanadu Portal to Catch Portal)

caverns.name: NW Twin Caldera & Caravan Skylight Vault (Nafkh al-Dukhān)
caverns.notes: Main caravan lava-tube skylight hall at +4,240 m on the WSW flank of the NW Twin (+6,480 m peak, +5,980 m crater floor), where caravaneers dash 1.8 km between Tube Segment I and Tube Segment II (biomes/twins/PLAN.md).

caverns.name: Sacred River Alph Pressurized Subglacial Reservoir
caverns.notes: Subglacial meltwater cavern on Xanadu's NE ice wall where geothermal pressure drives the bursting chasm fountain at the head of the Sacred River Alph (biomes/xanadu/NOTES.md).

name: Erebus Subglacial Ice-Cave & Catch Oasis Feeder Tube

branches.name: Lasso ('The Last Water') Southern Pass Feeder Tube

caverns.name: Kverkfjoll / Erebus Blue-Ice Fumarole Vaults
caverns.notes: Subglacial ice caves at +5,420 m beneath the +5,880 m SE Twin summit (`erebustwin`, biomes/twins/PLAN.md): blue-lit glacier vaults with 88 C boiling geysers and hollow fumarolic ice chimneys.

caverns.name: Bitta ('Bitter Water') Lava-Tube Spring Mouth
caverns.notes: Distal lava-tube spring surfacing at the fan toe of Oasis #4 (Bitta / al-Bitar, biomes/catch/PLAN.md), discharging mineralized volcanic brackish water.

caverns.name: Lasso ('The Last Water') Sub-Fan Cistern
caverns.notes: Southern lava-tube spring surfacing at Oasis #5 (Lasso / Lastu, biomes/catch/PLAN.md), the last water before the 7.3 km pass toward Strongbow.

name: Godthrone WNW Shield & Span-Wall Titanium Pyroduct

caverns.name: The Vacuum Glass Cathedral
caverns.notes: Giant collapsed titanium-basalt skylight gallery at ~13.8 km on the Godthrone's WNW vacuum shield, lined with metallic ilmenite-magnetite dripstone stalactites.

name: Godthrone North Shield & Talia-Saddle Ilmenite Tube

caverns.name: Ilmenite Pillar Vault
caverns.notes: Sealed sub-shield titanium-basalt lava tube chamber on the northern Godthrone slope where slow cooling precipitated 30-meter hexagonal columns of black ilmenite.

name: Godthrone SE Shield & Catch-Rim Radial Pyroduct

caverns.name: Sub-Glacial Sulfide Dome
caverns.notes: Geothermally heated titanium-basalt master tube on the SE Godthrone flank where residual volcanic heat melts subglacial domes into warm acidic sulfur lakes.

name: Godthrone SSW Shield & Brine-Lake Siphon Pyroduct

caverns.name: Red Riwa Subglacial Brine-Lake Conduit
caverns.notes: The drained brine lake's throat, under the caldera floor at ~3.6 km: the old reservoir emptied down it when Godshearth's caldera fell. The bloodfalls' brine now comes from the closed lake at 876,1440 (6,420 m), which the ice belt kept. biomes/godshearth/PLAN.md sections 1a and 8.

name: Neo-Ozarks Dolomite Karst & Porphyry-Vein Cavern System

caverns.name: Cathedral of the Red Porphyry Vein
caverns.notes: Vast phreatic dissolution hall in the Neo-Ozarks where groundwater dissolved cherty Gasconade-type dolomite along an impermeable dike wall of polished purple-red rhyolite porphyry.

caverns.name: Onyx Pillar & Chert-Bridge Labyrinth
caverns.notes: Multi-level dolomite and limestone cavern famous for 20-meter banded cave-onyx columns, suspended chert-breccia bridges, and copper-iron porphyry mineral veins.

caverns.name: The Shut-In Big Spring Resurgence
caverns.notes: First-magnitude karst spring cavern discharging emerald calcium-magnesium water through a breached porphyry shut-in gorge into the Neo-Ozark Porphyry Fork.

name: Epidote Cave

caverns.name: The Portal
caverns.notes: The cave's outer mouth at the head of the Portal Valley, 5,900 m (0.77 atm, EF), under the portal's ice.

caverns.name: The Marble Hall
caverns.notes: The upper level's great chamber under the crest (ground 11.8-12.1 km, about 6.2 km of rock overhead): white skarn marble dissolved from below, gypsum crust and cupolas, dry since the old water table fell.

caverns.name: The Inner Mouth
caverns.notes: The lower level's outlet on the Epidote-Steam Tarn's north shore, about 2,700 m, 30 m over the water: warm, CO2- and H2S-charged water and steam, sinter and mats round it.

notes: A hypogene cave (water from below, as Carlsbad and Lechuguilla) dissolved in the marble bands of the skarn along the Outland Gate fault (NNW-SSE), the only way into the sealed Epidote-Steam Tarn. The way in: the Portal Valley (1330,295 to 1331,302, floor 5,530-5,900 m, 14 km), then the cave. Floors (depth_m does not describe them): the upper level holds 5.6-5.9 km from the portal (5,900 m) to under the cauldron's rim (y 333); the lower level then falls about 2.9 km to the inner mouth (~2,700 m) in its last 6-8 km. Rock overhead peaks at about 6.4 km under the crest (1336,329, 12.1 km). No point of the walk stands over 5.9 km. A record only: nothing is carved. biomes/neouterwall/PLAN.md section 2a; the owner, 2026-11-09.
